title: panel-window: universal panel control (floating / docked / detached OS window); first consumer = file-open panel

decisions.text: Detached mechanism = window.open() of the same SPA, NO second AppCore process (answers owner's question, 2026-07-13). AppCore (c:\projects\Games\AppCore, FreePascal) hosts one WebView2 window via the webview/webview library (libwebview.dll); that library does NOT subscribe to NewWindowRequested (verified by grep over webview/core) -> WebView2's DEFAULT behavior applies: the runtime itself creates a child top-level popup window for window.open() — same browser process, same profile, same origin (shared localStorage + BroadcastChannel), and it dies with the host process. The child window opens '#/panel/<panelId>' (hash router) resolved against the current origin, so the SAME built SPA serves both windows in dev (quasar dev, plain browser popup) and prod (AppCore). Zero Pascal changes. A second AppCore process was REJECTED as heavy: AppMain.exe is built around launching bun + one window; it would need a window-only config mode plus a parent-PID watchdog, all in another repo. Fallback: if window.open returns null (popup blocker), stay floating and show a Quasar Notify.

Child-depends-on-parent (owner req. 2) is enforced on three levels: (a) the parent's pagehide handler broadcasts 'parent-gone'; the child then waits a grace period (~5s) for a fresh 'parent-hello' — this SURVIVES F5/hot-reload of the main window (the reloaded parent re-adopts the child) — and self-closes otherwise (window.close() is permitted for script-opened windows); (b) the parent heartbeats over the BroadcastChannel every ~2s; child silence-timeout (~6-8s) self-close covers a crashed/killed main tab where pagehide never fired; (c) the platform itself: when the AppCore host process exits, the WebView2 browser process and all its popup windows die. No server involvement.

Universal control (owner req. 3) = PanelWindow.vue + usePanelWindowState(panelId, opts). Generic state {open, mode: 'floating'|'left'|'right'|'top'|'bottom'|'detached', floatRect, dockSize, prevMode} persisted per panel under 'mindwave-panel-<id>-*' localStorage keys; opts lets a panel pass LEGACY key names so the file-open panel keeps its existing 'mindwave-fs-browser-*' keys (windowMode/dockSize/float/open) — backward compatible, no migration. The window chrome currently inlined in FileOpenDialog.vue moves into PanelWindow: titlebar (icon + title + drag), the collapsed dock-menu button (gains an 'Отдельное окно' item), close button, float corner-resizer and dock edge-resizer, plus the floating/docked mode classes and geometry style. Panel content and footer are slots. The fs-browser store keeps only browser domain state; its window-model fields move behind the shared composable.

Child-window content = a top-level route '/panel/:panelId' OUTSIDE MainLayout (no nav/header) rendering PanelHostPage.vue, which resolves the panel component from a PANEL REGISTRY contributed via module manifests — gnauralModule gains panels: [{id:'file-open', component, titleKey, icon}], collected in MindWaveCore/ui/src/modules/index.ts exactly like routes/settingsTabs. To make the same content usable in both windows, FileOpenDialog.vue splits into: PanelWindow (chrome, main window only) + FileOpenPanel.vue (body + footer: the browser UI, emits open/close) hosted by both FileOpenDialog-in-main and PanelHostPage-in-child. PanelHostPage sets document.title from titleKey so the OS window gets a proper caption.

Parent<->child bridge = BroadcastChannel('mw-panel:<id>') — same-origin is guaranteed by PW-D1. Message protocol: parent -> 'parent-hello' (on open + on reload), 'heartbeat', 'parent-gone' (pagehide), 'close-panel'; child -> 'child-ready', 'child-closed' (its own pagehide), 'panel-event' {name, payload}. Composables usePanelBridgeParent(id)/usePanelBridgeChild(id) own channel lifecycle + timers. Panel events carry domain actions: the file-open panel emits 'open' {path, kind}; the parent side re-emits it to AudioPage.handleExternalFileOpen — identical code path to an in-window open. Pinia stores are per-window instances (the child is a separate app instance); shared localStorage keeps preferences/favorites consistent, and navigation state is intentionally independent per window.

Detached lifecycle: choosing 'Отдельное окно' stores prevMode=current mode, sets mode='detached', calls window.open('#/panel/<id>', 'mw-panel-<id>', features from the persisted detached rect) and stops rendering the panel content in the main window (PanelWindow renders nothing while detached; the dock reflow releases the edge). User closes the CHILD window -> 'child-closed' -> panel returns to prevMode in the main window (panel stays open). Closing from the MAIN side (close-panel or open=false) closes the child too. On app start with open && mode='detached', auto-reopen is attempted ONCE (WebView2 default popup may be allowed without a user gesture; a browser blocker may return null) -> on failure fall back to floating + Notify (per PW-D1).

Detached window geometry persists like float/dock geometry: the child tracks resize events and polls screenX/screenY on its heartbeat tick (there is no move event) and writes 'mindwave-panel-<id>-detached-rect' to the shared localStorage; the next detach/auto-reopen passes width/height/left/top window features from it. Best-effort: if the platform ignores position features, the window still opens at its default spot.

Code placement: the universal control lives in the core repo — MindWaveCore/ui/src/components/panel/ (PanelWindow.vue, use-panel-window.ts, use-panel-bridge.ts, panel-registry.ts types) — exposed to module repos via a new '@panel' alias in quasar.config.ts + tsconfig.json paths, mirroring the existing '@protocol' alias. Module repos (GnauralCore) import via the alias, never via ../../ relative paths into another repo. Commits: MindWaveCore (core control, router, modules/index, aliases, docs) and GnauralCore (FileOpenDialog split, module manifest, store slimming) are staged separately per repo per the multi-repo rule.
